text.title: rust-tokio-async Procedure
text.summary: Step-by-step procedure to apply the rust-tokio-async methodology end-to-end.

step.name: classify-workload
step.action: Pick one of {try_join, spawn_blocking, buffer_unordered, JoinSet, select}.

step.name: set-concurrency-bound
step.action: Choose N <= pool_size; document the choice.

step.name: wrap-io-in-timeout
step.action: Wrap every reqwest/sqlx/grpc call with tokio::time::timeout.
step.decision-gate: If any call lacks a timeout, STOP and apply r6.

step.name: audit-await-safety
step.action: Verify no MutexGuard crosses .await; mark cancel-safety on select! branches.

step.name: settle-the-runtime-level-spec
step.input: Service workload, crate list, producer/consumer rates, per-call SLO, signal handling.
step.action: Fix the five runtime-level fields once per service, not per pattern: (a) pick `multi_thread` or `current_thread` and set `worker_threads` — reject the default runtime in production (r9); (b) inventory blocking calls and route each through `spawn_blocking` — reject inline blocking on async paths (r3); (c) set bounded `mpsc` capacity and document the overflow policy — reject unbounded channels (r10); (d) pick `timeout_default_ms` with per-call overrides allowed — reject bare network awaits (r6); (e) listen for `ctrl_c` and propagate via `CancellationToken` or a shutdown mpsc — reject an abrupt drop (r11).
step.output: Runtime-level spec: runtime_flavour, worker_threads, blocking_offload, channel_policy, timeout_default_ms, shutdown_signal. See templates/runtime-spec-example.json.
step.decision-gate: Any of the five rejects above still true - STOP; the per-pattern choices below are not worth making on a runtime that is already misconfigured.
